assessment_summary: The statement claims that in every tree with 2 to 7 vertices, any vertex with degree at least 2 is adjacent to a leaf. We can easily construct a counterexample using a path graph on 5 vertices ($P_5$). In $P_5$, the middle vertex has degree 2, but its two neighbors also have degree 2, meaning it is not adjacent to any leaves.
counterexample:
Let $T$ be the path graph $P_5$ with vertices $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ and edges $\{(1,2), (2,3), (3,4), (4,5)\}$. 
This is a tree on $n=5$ vertices, which satisfies $2 \le n \le 7$. 
The leaves of this tree (vertices of degree 1) are 1 and 5. 
Consider vertex 3. Its degree is 2, which is at least 2. 
Its neighbors are vertex 2 (degree 2) and vertex 4 (degree 2). 
Since neither of its neighbors is a leaf, vertex 3 is not adjacent to any leaf. This violates the conclusion of the statement.
